title: Baricitinib in WWOX-LoF
summary: A comparison of inflammatory signaling and trophic support for first myelin sheaths.

graph.evidence: Measured CSF exposure and different responses to the same cytokine.
graph.inference: A lower inflammatory marker leaves local function unresolved.
graph.hypothesis: Broad JAK inhibition may also remove protective glial signaling.
graph.experiment: Match inflammatory engagement and test new sheaths and conduction.

evidence: In Aicardi–Goutières syndrome, the median total CSF concentration was 19.55 nM across 11 samples from five people. In healthy whole-blood monocytes, IL-6/pSTAT1 and IL-6/pSTAT3 IC50 values were 39 and 161 nM.
inference: In cultured human sensory neurons, one nominal baricitinib concentration inhibited responses to both IL-6 and LIF. Separate mouse models give different developmental results after Stat3 loss.
hypothesis: A local inflammatory signal may amplify WWOX dysfunction. JAK inhibition could also attenuate CNTF/LIF support in the cells making first sheaths.
experiment: Compare baricitinib with one ligand-specific reference at matched inflammatory engagement. Measure local free drug, trophic responses, first sheaths per eligible axon and conduction.
limits: The pediatric clinical settings differ from WOREE. A local functional effect and preserved trophic response are required to raise research priority. Retain as a conditional laboratory probe.
